predictions.selection_reason: file stat comparison -> skip file extraction -> potential time-of-check-time-of-use race condition or bypass of intended file updates
predictions.source_summary: this.newer is set from user-provided opt.newer option; st.mtime comes from filesystem stat of existing file; entry.mtime comes from archive entry metadata
predictions.sink_summary: When condition is true, calls this[SKIPNEWER](entry) which skips file extraction by unpending and resuming the entry without writing
predictions.guard_summary: Time comparison acts as a guard to skip extraction if existing file is newer than archive entry; no additional validation of time values
predictions.risk_pattern: Time-of-check-time-of-use race condition: filesystem state (st.mtime) can change between lstat check and actual file operations, potentially allowing extraction of files that should be skipped
enclosing_conditions: Inside CHECKFS function called for file/directory entries
predictions.context_summary: The comparison determines whether to skip extracting an archive entry based on whether an existing file is newer than the archive version
unresolved_facts: How entry objects are created and populated from archive
Whether archive entry timestamps can be manipulated
External factors that could affect filesystem state between check and use

retrieval_query.mechanism_summary: Race condition in security decision based on file timestamp comparison for archive extraction
retrieval_query.missing_control: atomic operations or synchronization to prevent state change between check and use
retrieval_query.impact: bypass of file update policy, extraction of outdated or malicious files

top_sast_rules.description: Separately checking the state of a file before operating on it may allow an attacker to modify the file between the two operations.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal')
top_sast_rules.description: Extracting files from a malicious ZIP file, or similar type of archive, without validating that the destination file path is within the destination directory can allow an attacker to unexpectedly gain access to resources.
top_sast_rules.pattern: Look for security-sensitive operations that handle user input without proper validation or sanitization
top_sast_rules.remediation: Implement path validation using canonical paths. Reject paths containing '../' or similar traversal sequences.

top_sast_rules.cwe_name: Improper Link Resolution Before File Access ('Link Following')
top_sast_rules.description: File access follows a symlink, hardlink, or shortcut to an unintended resource.
top_sast_rules.pattern: cwe-59 symlink hardlink link-following symbolic-link file-link archive-extraction path-resolution file-overwrite race filesystem
top_sast_rules.remediation: Reject unsafe links and verify resolved file targets before access.
